answer.generated: Memory interleaving enhances the average rate of fetching words from main memory by distributing the memory system into multiple modules, ensuring that successive memory accesses are served by different modules, thereby allowing parallel access and increasing overall throughput. This technique is particularly beneficial in systems where consecutive memory addresses are accessed frequently, reducing contention and improving performance. Memory interleaving indirectly supports the concept of virtual memory by enhancing the effective speed and efficiency of the underlying physical memory, which is crucial for the seamless operation of virtual memory systems that manage larger address spaces than physically available memory through paging and segmentation mechanisms.
